PullRequest.Title: Fix permission bits in mock-policy-server file commands
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request addresses the permission bit settings for file-based configurations in the mock-policy-server to ensure compliance with SDK/runtime requirements. 

Changes made include:

- Updated macOS and Linux commands to explicitly set `root` ownership and mode `0644`, ensuring files are root-owned and not group/world-writable, even when overwriting existing files.
- No changes were made to Windows commands, as the runtime does not enforce equivalent ACL checks.
- Revised the README.md to reflect these updates.
- Applied consistent fixes to both UI-generated commands in `app.ts` and the control API in `server.ts`.

Validation has been completed successfully, confirming that the changes meet the necessary requirements.

Scenarios.Scenario: Editing Managed Settings in the mock-policy-server UI and copying a generated deployment command
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each editor input synchronously parses/stringifies the current JSON, rebuilds three command strings, and assigns them to existing DOM text nodes. The diff only adds a fixed amount of shell syntax to the macOS and Linux strings; no new asynchronous work or expensive boundary blocks editing.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Command construction still scales linearly with the existing JSON body because the body is embedded once per platform; the diff adds constant-sized prefixes only. There are exactly two affected command strings per render after endpoint filtering.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single browser event-loop execution per input event; existing debounced server save remains unchanged and the changed command construction does not add requests or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved in command generation. Existing local draft persistence and save debouncing are unchanged; cold and warm behavior are equivalent for the changed work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the input listener and renderFileDeploy call path: all changed UI work is local string construction and DOM text replacement, with no introduced boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact body sizes and typing rates vary, but the added work is a few hundred fixed characters per render and does not alter body-copy cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff slightly increases constant allocation and DOM text size but does not add input-scaled work, extra renders, or a boundary on the UI critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Fetching GET /api/file-deployment from the control API
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The request synchronously reads in-memory state, stringifies the managed-settings body, constructs the response object, serializes it through the existing sendJson path, and sends it over the existing HTTP request. The changed command text contributes only fixed response bytes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Return the generated deployment metadata and commands over the existing HTTP control endpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One HTTP response per explicit API request; three platform command entries are grouped in that response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same endpoint and one-response cardinality existed before the diff, with shorter macOS and Linux command strings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing response send is on the request critical path; the diff adds only constant response bytes and no additional calls.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Serialization remains linear in the managed-settings body and one grouped response per request. The diff adds a constant number of shell-command characters independent of body size or endpoint count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous command-generation operation per incoming request; no changed limiter, queue, fan-out, or new concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No server cache is used for this endpoint before or after the diff; state is read from the in-memory map on every explicit request.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the direct route-to-getFileDeployment call path and unchanged response structure.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Request frequency is developer-driven, but even repeated requests add only fixed bytes and fixed string work beyond the pre-diff response.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. No new network boundary or fan-out is introduced, and serialization/allocation growth is constant.

Scenarios.Scenario: Running a generated macOS or Linux install command on a client machine
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A developer explicitly runs one command. It serially creates the directory, creates a temporary file, writes the JSON, sets ownership and mode, atomically renames it, and removes any leftover temporary file on exit; all steps must finish before deployment completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke sudo and a shell that runs mktemp, cat, chown, chmod, mv, and trap cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One manually invoked shell pipeline per deployment; a constant set of serial commands, with no per-policy fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The generated command used sudo tee to write the single destination file directly after mkdir.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The extra shell commands are on the one-shot deployment critical path, but their cardinality is fixed and they operate on a single small configuration file.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Generated install commands in scripts/mock-policy-server/public/app.ts and scripts/mock-policy-server/server.ts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a temporary file, write one JSON document, change ownership and permissions, atomically rename it, and clean up the temporary path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One destination directory check, one temporary file, one body write, two metadata changes, one rename, and at most one cleanup attempt per manual deployment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Previously mkdir and tee performed a direct write to the destination without temporary-file metadata operations or rename.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These fixed serial filesystem operations complete before the command returns; they do not scale with policy count beyond the existing body-write bytes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The data write remains linear in the JSON body size; all newly added subprocess and filesystem operations have constant cardinality per explicit deployment.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All operations are intentionally serialized with shell &&; no concurrent subprocess or I/O burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used. Re-running the command repeats one bounded deployment both before and after the diff; warm filesystem state only makes mkdir a no-op-like directory check.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the diff introduces extra serial commands and filesystem operations, based directly on the generated shell text; high confidence that invocation is manual and one-shot from the README and API note.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem and process startup latency varies by client, but this is a manually invoked one-file setup operation rather than a recurring product path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The bounded one-shot overhead is necessary to establish required ownership/mode and atomic replacement, with no realistic multiplicity or concurrency amplification.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete three-file diff and traced UI rendering, API generation/serialization, and manual command execution. The PR adds fixed-size command text and bounded one-shot filesystem/subprocess work, without new hot-path fan-out, unbounded retention, cache regression, or meaningful critical-path scaling.
